key_insight: OSReward shows that even top vision-language model judges are systematically too lenient on computer-use trajectories, so they are not yet reliable as drop-in reward models.
engineering_relevance: For CUA systems, training, evaluation, and data curation need cheaper and more stable reward signals than frontier VLM judges currently provide.
method: Built OSReward, a cross-platform benchmark with human-verified instructions and multi-stage human-labeled ground-truth verdicts.
Created OSReward-Hard for genuinely difficult cases and OSReward-Multi for fine-grained efficiency/alignment scoring.
Trained OS-Shepherd-100K and open OS-Shepherd models (9B/35B) to provide low-cost trajectory judgments.
evidence_signal: The benchmark supports the most comprehensive evaluation to date, revealing a systematic leniency bias in state-of-the-art VLM judges and a cost-quality gap between frontier and open models.
watch_item: Reliability depends on high-quality trajectory labels, so deployment should account for annotation standards, domain shift across platforms, and the risk of lenient false positives.
paper_title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
